# wts-data-table

> Accessible, dependency-free, framework-agnostic data table for TypeScript
> and JavaScript. It provides a DOM-free headless core, a semantic DOM
> controller, and an optional Web Component with no runtime dependencies.

Current stable package version: `1.1.0`.
Migration notice: card view requires a verified `card-view` entitlement from
1.1.0 onward. Existing 1.0.x releases remain unchanged; standard tables need no key.

## Entry points

- `wts-data-table`: `DataTable`, `DataTableCore`, `createDataTables`,
  `createDataTableCore`, and all public types
- `wts-data-table/base`: truly modular semantic renderer with sorting,
  filtering, and pagination in core and executable optional feature runtimes
- `wts-data-table/base-runtime`: contracts for third-party composable renderer
  modules, per-instance hooks, row windows, and host/controller access
- `wts-data-table/base.css`: structural and optional-runtime styles for base
- `wts-data-table/complete`: explicit compatibility alias for the root renderer
- `wts-data-table/card-view`: licensed responsive table/card controller; requires a verified `card-view` entitlement and actual host origin for origin-bound keys
- `wts-data-table/core`: DOM-free `DataTableCore` and core types
- `wts-data-table/crud`: headless CRUD transactions, REST adapter, and
  dialog/bubble/inline multi-row editor
- `wts-data-table/data-source`: abortable, debounced, cached remote loading
- `wts-data-table/element`: `WtsDataTableElement`,
  `defineDataTableElement`, and `WTS_DATA_TABLE_TAG_NAME`
- `wts-data-table/edit-history`: atomic batch edits and bounded undo/redo
- `wts-data-table/export`: PDF, print, XLSX, CSV, JSON, and clipboard helpers
- `wts-data-table/feature-system`: feature validation and module types
- `wts-data-table/features/*`: executable selection, grouping, editing,
  responsive, virtualization, SearchPanes, export, pivot, ColumnControl, and
  sticky modules
- `wts-data-table/lite`: compact semantic renderer for sorting, filtering,
  pagination, grouping, selection, responsive overflow, and virtualization
- `wts-data-table/lite.css`: compact renderer styles
- `wts-data-table/i18n`: immutable locale packs, negotiation, renderer option
  adapters, Accept-Language parsing, and Intl formatter helpers
- `wts-data-table/locales/*`: exact en, fr, de, es, ar, hi, ja, zh-CN, and
  pt-BR locale packs; the aggregate `/locales` entry is optional
- `wts-data-table/persistence`: versioned storage and URL-state helpers
- `wts-data-table/pivot`: DOM-free pivot and cross-tab aggregation models
- `wts-data-table/plugin`: import-scoped definitions, manifests, dependency
  resolution, compatibility validation, catalogs, and per-table installation
- `wts-data-table/plugin-manifest.schema.json`: JSON Schema for plug-in
  manifest API v1
- `wts-data-table/presets`: lite, standard, and complete feature arrays
- `wts-data-table/saved-views`: versioned named-view repository
- `wts-data-table/server`: shared rows/facets/cursor transport with request and
  response mapping, retries, caching, cancellation, validation, and telemetry
- `wts-data-table/server-db`: injected Prisma, Knex, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and
  SQLite processing with facets, summaries, options, and signed keyset cursors;
  compatibility entry retained through 1.x
- `@wts-data-table/protocol`: separately published protocol v1 types, parser,
  JSON Schema, response validation, and cross-language fixtures
- `@wts-data-table/server`: separately published Node backend with Express,
  GraphQL, Fetch, SQL, Prisma, and Knex integrations
- `wts-data-table/theme`: semantic class/wrapper adapter helpers and types
- `wts-data-table/themes/*`: Bootstrap 5, Bulma, Foundation, Fomantic UI,
  jQuery UI, and Tailwind class presets with no framework stylesheet imports
- `wts-data-table/themes`: aggregate preset registry, CSS detection, and theme
  resolution helpers
- `wts-data-table/styles.css`: UI styles for the DOM and custom-element layers

## Licensed advanced features

Advanced capabilities ship in the same `wts-data-table` package under normal
feature-named subpaths. There is no separate Pro package and no `/premium`
namespace. Representative entries are `wts-data-table/remote`,
`wts-data-table/search`, `wts-data-table/worker-engine`,
`wts-data-table/live-data`, `wts-data-table/pivot-controller`,
`wts-data-table/formula-engine`, `wts-data-table/collaboration-client`,
`wts-data-table/governance-client`, and `wts-data-table/report-designer`.

Executable advanced factories require a signed grant created with
`verifyDataTableLicense()` from the root or `wts-data-table/license` entry.
Pass the grant as `license` in the factory options and pass `origin` when the
entitlement is origin-bound. Plain API keys do not unlock these APIs. See
`ADVANCED_FEATURES.md` and `docs/advanced/ROADMAP.md`.

All JavaScript entry points are SSR-safe to import. The element entry registers
`<wts-data-table>` only when a `CustomElementRegistry` exists.

## Modular distribution

Use `DataTable` from `wts-data-table/base` and exact
`wts-data-table/features/*` imports for true renderer modularity. Each module
owns executable render/event/lifecycle hooks and is absent from the bundle
when omitted. Duplicate names, missing dependencies, conflicts, and missing
base runtimes fail early. Sorting, filtering, and pagination need no module.
`standardPreset()` adds selection and responsive behavior;
`completePreset()` adds all first-party runtime modules.

The root and `/complete` entries are the unchanged batteries-included
compatibility renderer. `/lite` remains a fixed compact read-heavy renderer.
Measured minified consumer bundles are about 13.5 KB gzip for bare `/base`,
14.5 KB for standard, 21.4 KB for modular complete, and 49.6 KB for the
compatibility renderer. Official React, Vue, and Angular packages expose
components/composables for both base and compatibility renderers. Run
`wts-data-table setup --renderer base --preset ...` or `--features ...` to
generate imports.

## Plug-in ecosystem

`defineDataTablePlugin()` validates a serializable API-v1 manifest and a
feature factory. `DataTablePluginRegistry` is local to the consumer and never
loads packages or styles by name. `resolve()` orders registered transitive
dependencies, validates API/WTS/dependency versions, renderers, conflicts,
cycles, options, and feature duplication, then returns features for one table.
Manifests can advertise explicit CSS exports; consumers import them normally.
Use the `wts-data-table-plugin` npm keyword and the published manifest schema.
Catalog helpers produce deterministic metadata and never execute remote code.

## Internationalization

Use an exact `wts-data-table/locales/<code>` import and the renderer-specific
option helper from `/i18n`. Packs configure labels, filter operators, core
collation locale, and direction together. Arabic is RTL. Locale negotiation
supports BCP 47 aliases, subtag fallback, browser arrays, and weighted HTTP
headers. Custom definitions inherit frozen English fallbacks. Intl formatter
helpers cover numbers, dates, date/time, lists, relative time, and plurals
without bundling CLDR data.

## Styling API

`wts-data-table/styles.css` exposes 78 supported `--wts-table-*` custom
properties. The API covers the core palette, typography, density, cell and
header spacing, focus/editing/error states, controls and filters, pagination,
column menus, pinned columns and rows, row drag controls, aggregate summary
footers, grouping, tree rows, detail panels, scrollbars, and layer ordering.
Override tokens on the controller root, the custom-element host, or an
ancestor. Component tokens derive from core palette tokens by default.

`--wts-table-tree-indent`, `--wts-table-expander-size`,
`--wts-table-detail-background`, and `--wts-table-detail-padding` customize
hierarchy and master-detail presentation. `--wts-table-row-controls-width`,
`--wts-table-row-drag-handle-color`,
`--wts-table-row-pinned-background`, and
`--wts-table-row-pinned-shadow` customize ordering and pinned rows.
`--wts-table-summary-background`, `--wts-table-summary-text`,
`--wts-table-summary-font-weight`, `--wts-table-summary-border`, and
`--wts-table-summary-shadow` customize semantic aggregate footers.
`--wts-pin-left`,
`--wts-pin-right`, `--wts-group-depth`, `--wts-row-depth`,
`--wts-selection-inline-start`, `--wts-control-inline-start`,
`--wts-summary-sticky-count`, and `--wts-summary-sticky-index` are
renderer-owned internal variables and are not part of the supported
customization API. `data-theme="auto"` supplies dark palette overrides while
preserving developer overrides.

Host-framework theme presets apply classes from CSS already loaded by the
application; they never import or bundle that framework. The WTS stylesheet is
in the low-priority `wts-data-table` cascade layer. Tailwind must scan the
installed `dist/themes/tailwind.js` entry so its utility classes are generated.
Use `theme: 'auto'` for active CSS detection and default fallback, or a named
string for validation. `getThemeStatus()` reports resolution and `setTheme()`
switches at runtime. `<wts-data-table theme="auto">` is declarative shorthand.
`npx wts-data-table setup` detects dependencies and prints or generates setup.

Columns accept `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, and `enableResizing`. The DOM controller
exposes constrained `getColumnSize()`, `setColumnSize()`,
`autoSizeColumn()`, and `autoSizeColumns()` methods; double-clicking a resize
handle and the header menu also autosize.

## Scalable selection and bulk actions

Set `selectionMode: 'multiple'` and `bulkActions: true` for the built-in
selected count, all-filtered selection, and clear controls. An options object
accepts async `actions`, custom DOM/SVG `content`, `disabled`, `renderSummary`,
`showClear`, `showSelectAllFiltered`, `visibleWhen`, and `onError`.
`selectAllFilteredRows()` uses a compact all-filtered scope plus
`rowSelectionExcluded`; use `getSelectedRowCount()` and
`getRowSelectionState()` rather than counting `state.rowSelection`. The action
context contains both explicit IDs and exclusion IDs for server APIs.

Web Components expose `bulk-actions` and `bulk-select-all-filtered`; assign
callback actions through `element.options.bulkActions`.

## SearchPanes, ranges, and AutoFill

`searchPanes: true | DataTableSearchPanesOptions` adds a collapsible faceted
sidebar with local or abortable remote facets, live counts, preselection,
uniqueness thresholds, and cascading multi-value filters.
Use `cellSelection: true` plus `selectCell`, `selectCellRange`,
`selectColumnRange`, `selectRowRange`, `getCellSelection`, and
`clearCellSelection` for framework-neutral range state. `autoFill: true` adds
the editable fill handle; `autoFillTo(target, 'copy' | 'series')` exposes the
same copy and numeric-series behavior programmatically.

## Layout, grouped headers, and temporal controls

`layout` places `toolbar`, `searchPanes`, `pagination`, callback content, or
plugins in `topStart`, `topEnd`, `bottomStart`, and `bottomEnd`.
`registerDataTableFeature()` owns global plugins; instance `plugins` override
matching names. Plugins render direct DOM/SVG content and can implement
`init`/`destroy`.

`buttons` unifies copy/CSV/Excel/PDF/print, column visibility, nested
collections, saved-view commands, and application actions. Per-column
`columnControls` composes ordered sorting, grouping, pinning, ordering, sizing,
visibility, table, and custom controls in the three-dot header menu.

Columns accept `headerGroup: string | readonly string[]` for semantic nested
header rows. `date-range`, `datetime-range`, and `time-range` filters use
native controls. Editable columns accept `date`, `datetime-local`, and `time`
editors with `min`, `max`, and `step`.

## PDF, print, and CRUD

`exportDataTableToPdf`, `downloadDataTablePdf`,
`createDataTablePrintHtml`, and `printDataTable` share the standard visible
columns, filtered/page/selected scopes, and value transforms.

`createDataTableCrudController` from `wts-data-table/crud` provides serialized
create/update/delete operations, async adapters, validation, optimistic
updates, rollback, and state/error callbacks. `createDataTableCrudEditor`
optionally adds dialog, anchored bubble, or inline workflows with typed/custom
fields, direct DOM/SVG actions, and mixed-value-aware multi-row editing.
`createDataTableRestCrudAdapter` supplies injectable JSON backend operations.

Columns can return orthogonal `{ display, sort, filter, export }` values.
Use `sortSequence` to configure a column's header cycle and `sortNulls` to
keep nullish values automatic, first, or last in both sort directions.
Use column `sortType` for built-in boolean, currency, date, file-size,
formatted-number, HTML-text, IP-address, month-year, natural, number,
numeric-comma, percentage, semantic-version, or text comparators. Applications can add
named comparators with `registerDataTableSortType` or per-table `sortTypes`.
`stickyHeader` and `stickyFooter` work with or without virtualization and
coordinate with measured grouped/filter headers, summary rows, pinned
columns, editable cells, and two-axis scrolling.
Set sticky section `mode: 'window'` (or `sticky-mode="window"`) to follow
document scrolling; the default container mode is required for virtualization.

## Basic DOM API

```ts
const table = new DataTable<Person>({
  element: '#table',
  data,
  columns: [
    { accessor: 'name', header: 'Name' },
    { accessor: 'age', header: 'Age', align: 'end' },
  ],
  getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  editing: true,
  initialState: { grouping: ['team'] },
  selectionMode: 'multiple',
  columnFilters: { mode: 'collapsible', initiallyExpanded: false },
  showColumnManager: true,
  showGrouping: true,
  pagination: {
    mode: 'pages',
    siblingCount: 1,
    boundaryCount: 1,
    showPageJump: true,
  },
  responsive: { breakpoint: 720, details: 'inline' },
  virtualization: { height: 480, rowHeight: 48, overscan: 6 },
});
```

The controller renders a native table with accessible sorting, search,
pagination, selection, loading, and empty states. Call `destroy()` during view
cleanup.

## Column filter row

Use `columnFilters: 'hidden' | 'always' | 'collapsible'` or an options object
with `mode` and `initiallyExpanded`. Collapsible mode adds an accessible
funnel toggle to the final visible header and preserves active filters while
the row is closed. `getColumnFiltersExpanded()` inspects the presentation and
`setColumnFiltersExpanded(expanded)` controls it.

The legacy `showColumnFilters: true` maps to always-visible mode. A modern
`columnFilters` value takes precedence. Columns continue to opt out
individually with `enableFiltering: false`.

`globalFilterOptions` selects `contains`, `equals`, `starts-with`, or `regex`
matching and configures case sensitivity and trimming without changing the
controlled `globalFilter` string.
Structured column and advanced filters also accept `operator: 'regex'` and
`caseSensitive`. Async/server requests include normalized filtering metadata
so remote adapters can mirror global matching semantics.
Column `columnFilterOptions` makes plain header-filter strings use a configured
contains, exact, prefix, or regex mode and transports that configuration too.

## Faceted and advanced filtering

Set `advancedFiltering: true` for removable chips and a visual query builder,
or pass `{ showBuilder, showChips }`. `state.advancedFilter` is a typed nested
tree of `and`/`or` groups and conditions using the standard structured-filter
operators. Control it with `setAdvancedFilter(group)` and clear every filter
surface with `clearFilters()`.

`getColumnFacet(columnId, limit?)` returns unique values with counts plus
minimum, maximum, and total metadata. Facets exclude the target column's own
column filter. Advanced state is included in async request keys, persistence,
saved views, URL state, and the `advanced-filter` change reason.

## Adaptive pagination

Use `pagination: true` for the default numbered paginator, `false` to hide it,
or an options object with `mode: 'pages' | 'simple'`, `siblingCount`,
`boundaryCount`, `showFirst`, `showPrevious`, `showPageNumbers`,
`showPageStatus`, `showNext`, `showLast`, `showPageJump`, `showPageSize`, and
`showSummary`. Numbered pagination uses a compact ellipsis window and marks
the active page with `aria-current="page"`.

Customize `controls.first`, `previous`, `page`, `ellipsis`, `next`, and `last`
with direct or callback `content`, `className`, `ariaLabel`, and `title`
values. Content accepts strings and DOM Nodes including `HTMLElement`,
`SVGElement`, and `Text`. Static Nodes are cloned; callbacks receive the
owning `document` plus page, active, and disabled state. At narrow widths,
page numbers, first/last controls, and the jump input collapse to compact
page status.

The legacy `showPagination` option remains supported. An explicit
`pagination` value takes precedence. Manual pagination uses the same UI and
derives its page count from `rowCount`.

With `showColumnManager: true`, every visible header gets a three-dot menu for
sorting, pinning, moving, hiding, and resetting width. The final header menu
also restores hidden columns and resets the full layout. Header grips support
drag-and-drop ordering. Columns can opt out with `enableReordering: false` or
`enableHiding: false`.

Column menus close on outside pointer press, Escape, and actions by default.
Use `columnMenu: true | false | { closeOnAction?, closeOnEscape?,
closeOnOutsideClick? }` to enable, disable, or customize them. The Web
Component mirrors these settings with `column-menu-close-on-action`,
`column-menu-close-on-escape`, and
`column-menu-close-on-outside-click`.

## Grouping and aggregation

Set `state.grouping` or call `setGrouping(columnIds)` for nested row groups.
Group rows expand by default and explicit choices live in
`state.groupExpansion`. Use `getGroupedRowModel()` for the nested tree or
`getDisplayRowModel()` for visible group headers plus expanded leaves;
`getRowModel()` remains the flat leaf-row API.

Columns accept `aggregation: 'count' | 'sum' | 'average' | 'min' | 'max'` or
a custom aggregation function, and `enableGrouping: false` disables grouping.
With `showGrouping: true`, headers can be dragged into a compact grouping bar.
Header menus also expose group/ungroup actions. Grouping participates in
saved views, persistence, URL state, and async data-source requests.

## Expandable rows, tree data, and master-detail

Supply `getSubRows(row)` for hierarchical data. Tree rows expose `depth`,
`parentId`, and `subRows`; filtering retains matching descendant paths,
sorting runs independently per sibling level, and pagination counts root
rows. `getRowModel()` returns paginated roots and `getDisplayRowModel()`
returns the visible flattened tree.

Use `rowExpansion: true | { allowMultiple?, expandOnRowClick?,
showControls?, renderToggle?, renderDetailPanel? }`. Toggle and detail
callbacks return safe text, a DOM Node, or another `DataTableCellContent`.
Control state through
`setRowExpanded`, `toggleRowExpanded`, `expandAllRows`, `collapseAllRows`,
and `state.rowExpansion`. `getRowCanExpand` supports server-loaded parents.

Expansion is persisted and sent to data sources with the `row-expansion`
change reason. Web Component JSON trees use `tree-children-key`; the element
also exposes `row-expansion`, `expand-on-row-click`,
`row-expansion-controls`, and `row-expansion-multiple`.

## Responsive columns

Set `responsive: { breakpoint: 720, details: 'inline' }` on the DOM
controller. Columns accept `responsivePriority` (lower values stay visible
longer) and `responsive: 'always' | 'auto' | 'never'`. Collapsed values are
available through accessible inline details or a popover dialog. With
virtualization, inline details automatically use the popover mode.

Responsive hiding is transient and does not modify core
`columnVisibility`. Inspect it with `getResponsiveHiddenColumns()`, subscribe
with `onResponsiveChange`, or listen for
`wts-data-table-responsive-change`.

## Inline editing

Set `editing: true` and add `editable: true` or an editable options object to
columns. Built-in editors are inferred from `dataType` and `filterOptions`.
Editable options support `type`, `parse`, sync/async `validate`, immutable
`setValue`, and a custom `editor(context)` HTMLElement.

Editing supports Enter/F2 and double-click activation, Escape cancellation,
Arrow-key navigation, Tab commit-and-move, Shift+Arrow range selection, and
TSV copy/paste. ARIA grid semantics are added only while editing is enabled.
The initial first-cell tab stop stays visually and semantically unselected
until the user focuses, clicks, navigates, or edits a cell. Cell selection is
separate from checkbox-based row selection.

`onEditCommit(context)` persists an optimistic update. A rejected promise
rolls the value back and displays an accessible error. Use
`getDirtyCells()` and `clearDirtyCells()` for dirty tracking.

Editing events are `wts-data-table-before-edit` (cancelable),
`wts-data-table-cell-change`, `wts-data-table-edit-commit`,
`wts-data-table-edit-cancel`, and `wts-data-table-edit-error`.

## Headless API

```ts
const core = createDataTableCore({ data, columns, getRowId });
core.subscribe((state, reason) => render(state, reason));
core.toggleSorting('name');
core.setGrouping(['team']);
core.setGlobalFilter('engineering');
core.setColumnFilter('status', 'active');
core.setColumnVisibility('notes', false);
core.setColumnSize('name', 280);
core.pinColumn('name', 'left');
core.resetColumnLayout();
core.setPageIndex(1);
core.setPageSize(25);
core.toggleRowSelected('row-id');
core.getRowModel();
```

`DataTableCore` never reads the DOM. It supports custom accessors, filters and
comparators; stable multi-sort; client pagination; single or multiple
selection; and immutable state snapshots.

## Async data

`createDataTableDataSourceController({ table, dataSource })` subscribes to
query-state changes and provides debouncing, abort cancellation, stale-result
protection, bounded TTL caching, refresh/invalidate methods, and status events.

`createDataTableCursorDataSourceController()` supports opaque cursor pages,
append loading, optional totals, duplicate-boundary removal, cancellation,
query-change resets, and `getCursorState()`. Call `loadMore()` directly or use
the SSR-safe `observeDataTableInfiniteScroll()` sentinel helper.

## Saved views

`createDataTableSavedViewStore()` saves, lists, renames, applies, and removes
versioned named table states using localStorage or a custom storage adapter.

## Manual server processing

Set `manualFiltering`, `manualSorting`, and/or `manualPagination` to true.
Respond to `onStateChange`, fetch rows, and call `setData(rows, total)`.
`rowCount` controls the page count in manual pagination mode.

## Web Component

```ts
import 'wts-data-table/element';
element.data = rows;
element.columns = columns;
element.options = { getRowId, selectionMode: 'multiple' };
```

Basic object rows and property columns also accept JSON `data` and `columns`
attributes. Function accessors and cell renderers must be assigned as
properties.

Attributes `responsive`, `responsive-breakpoint`, and `responsive-details`
configure adaptive rendering. JSON column objects accept `responsive` and
`responsivePriority`.

Attributes `editing`, `edit-activation`, `edit-navigation`, and `edit-paste`
configure editing. JSON columns accept `editable: true` or an object with a
built-in editor `type`; assign validators and custom editors as properties.

Attributes `pagination-mode`, `pagination-boundary-count`,
`pagination-sibling-count`, `pagination-first-last`,
`pagination-first`, `pagination-previous`, `pagination-page-numbers`,
`pagination-page-status`, `pagination-next`, `pagination-last`,
`pagination-page-jump`, `pagination-page-size`, and `pagination-summary`
configure the adaptive paginator. Assign control Nodes through
`element.options.pagination.controls`.

Attributes `column-filters="hidden|always|collapsible"` and
`column-filters-expanded` configure the filter row. The legacy
`show-column-filters` attribute remains supported.

Attributes `advanced-filtering`, `advanced-filter-builder`, and `filter-chips`
configure advanced filtering.

## Events

- `wts-data-table-state-change`: bubbling event with
  `{ instance, state, reason }`
- `wts-data-table-responsive-change`: bubbling event with
  `{ instance, hiddenColumnIds }`
- `wts-data-table-error`: invalid Web Component JSON configuration with
  `{ attribute, error }`

String cell output is inserted with `textContent`. Return a `Node` from a
column `cell` renderer for trusted rich UI.

## Official framework wrappers

`@wts-data-table/react`, `@wts-data-table/vue`, and
`@wts-data-table/angular` keep their framework runtime and `wts-data-table` as
peer dependencies. They update row input in place, remount when the options
object changes, expose the complete `DataTable<T>` controller, skip DOM work
during SSR, and destroy on unmount. Vue also exports
`createWtsDataTableVue<T>` and `useWtsDataTable<T>`; Angular's component is
standalone for Angular 17–22.

Wrapper v1.1 adds framework-owned content and controlled state. React uses
`renderers.columns[columnId]` for cell/header/filter/menu functions plus
detail/empty/loading/footer renderers and `state` / `onStateChange`. Vue uses
generic or `{kind}-{columnId}` scoped slots and `v-model:state`. Angular uses
the standalone `wtsDataTableCell`, `wtsDataTableHeader`,
`wtsDataTableFilter`, `wtsDataTableMenu`, `wtsDataTableDetail`,
`wtsDataTableEmpty`, `wtsDataTableLoading`, and `wtsDataTableFooter`
directives plus `[(state)]`. Renderer roots and embedded views are reclaimed
after redraw and teardown.
